chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no 'ila' (oath of abstention) for a man from the woman with whom he enjoys temporary marriage.

key_terms.إِيلاَء: Ila: An oath taken by a husband to abstain from sexual relations with his wife for a specified period.
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُ بِهَا: Yatamatta'u biha: He enjoys her; refers to the act of temporary marriage (Mut'ah) where a man marries a woman for a specified duration.

ai.seo_question: Does the ruling of Ila apply to temporary marriage (Mut'ah)?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifies that the specific legal mechanism of 'ila' (oath of abstention) does not apply to temporary marriage (mut'ah), distinguishing it from permanent marriage where such oaths trigger a waiting period and potential divorce. This ruling highlights the distinct jurisprudential framework of mut'ah, where the fixed duration supersedes the indefinite waiting period associated with 'ila'. It underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in adapting marital laws to the unique temporal nature of mut'ah.
